newsitem.title: CHINA: China to keep deposit interest income tax-free.
newsitem.headline: China to keep deposit interest income tax-free.

text.p: China will not levy taxes on income from interest on bank accounts for fear it would reduce savings in the banking system and boost the illegal credit market, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.
"It is not suitable for China to levy taxes on the interest of bank deposits in the near future," the newspaper quoted a report by the State Statistical Bureau as saying.
A tax on interest would hit at economic growth by making individual deposits -- a major source of lending funds for banks -- less attractive, the report said.
Such measures would also help to fuel illegal financial activities, the report said.

Reform of China's financial system has lagged behind changes in other sectors and a flourishing underground credit market has sprung up as many firms find themselves unable to obtain badly-needed capital from state banks.
Many illegal financial institutions collect funds from grass-roots trade unions and individuals and lend the money at higher than official rates.
